chunks: Muḥammad ibn Aḥmad ibn Yaḥyā narrated from al-Ḥusayn ibn Ibrāhīm al-Hamdānī, who said:

I wrote along with Muḥammad ibn Yaḥyā asking whether the executor of a will may purchase something from the estate of the deceased when it is sold among bidders, each increasing the bid, and take it for himself.
So he said: “It is permissible if he purchases it properly.”

key_terms.الْوَصِيِّ: the executor of the will or estate administrator
key_terms.مَالِ الْمَيِّتِ: the property or estate belonging to the deceased

ai.seo_question: Can an executor buy property from the estate of the deceased if it is sold to the highest bidder?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling about an executor purchasing from the deceased's estate. It indicates that such a purchase is permissible when the transaction is carried out properly and validly, implying fairness and correctness in the sale process.

en.bab-ul-qaim-publications: Hadith.5514 - Muhammad ibn Ahmad ibn Yahya narrated from Al-Husayn ibn Ibrahim Al-Hamdani, who said:

I wrote along with Muhammad ibn Yahya asking whether the executor of a will is permitted to purchase something from the deceased's estate when it is sold to the highest bidder and take it for himself.
Imam (as) replied: "It is permissible if he purchases it properly."
